source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.address: 2215 Martin Avenue, Santa Clara County, CA
profile.reading: Prime Santa Clara sits at 2215 Martin Avenue in Santa Clara County, California, internally coded SJC03 by the operator, one of three separate buildings that make up Prime Data Centers Silicon Valley portfolio in this dataset. Per Prime own site, SJC03 is designed for 9 megawatts of capacity across 79,000 square feet and is listed in development status rather than fully operational or leased. Prime own Silicon Valley locations page describes the broader portfolio there as five buildings totaling 57 megawatts, 540,000 square feet, and 17 data halls across 13 acres, of which SJC03 is one component alongside the separately mapped SJC02 and SJC04 buildings elsewhere in this dataset, roughly a kilometer away on Comstock Street. No tenant is disclosed for SJC03, and no year-built figure is published. Prime Data Centers was founded in 2017 in California and is now headquartered at 400 North Ervay Street in Dallas, Texas. The company describes itself on its own site as majority founder-owned, a description that does not claim institutional private equity or infrastructure fund majority ownership, though it does not rule out unnamed minority capital partners either. Founder and CEO Nicholas Laag leads the company alongside CFO Ulrich Pelz and other named executives. Prime describes its overall footprint as 28 data centers across 13 campuses with a stated pipeline exceeding 4 gigawatts, spanning Austin, Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Sacramento, and Silicon Valley in North America, plus Frankfurt and Madrid in Europe and a newly announced site in Esbjerg, Denmark. Santa Clara sits at the heart of Silicon Valley, one of the most constrained and expensive data center land and power markets in the country, a dynamic reflected in Prime decision to develop a multi-building, phased portfolio there rather than one single large campus.

reading.body:
Prime Santa Clara publishes 57 MW of IT capacity across 540,000 square feet in Silicon Valley, making it the third-largest facility by published power in California and representing 16 percent of the state's 365 MW of published data center IT load. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 57 MW of IT load translates to roughly 1,425 racks, assuming full utilization for compute-intensive workloads. The campus holds SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, and PCI DSS certifications, qualifying it for security-sensitive workloads and regulated computing.

California has mapped 103 data center facilities but publishes power figures for only 11. Prime Santa Clara ranks among the handful of sites in the state with disclosed capacity, placing it in a narrow set of campuses whose scale is known. The operator, Prime Data Centers, operates 28 facilities across 13 global campuses and reports a 4-plus gigawatt expansion pipeline, but individual facility opening dates and build-out timelines are not published.

The site's location in Santa Clara County, the heart of the technology industry, positions it for short hauls to major compute demand centers. Whether this campus is acquiring new load or serving existing tenants is not published. The grid serving Silicon Valley is not specified in the available data.
